items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: he wrote all the music, we recorded in Miami, went to Germany after the record came out, did a three week tour

ctx.x: Absolutely, yeah. They didn’t want to play his charts. He wasn’t happy there. This is the first time on tape folks, maybe I’ll get assassinated for this. The guys in the band didn’t want him there. Look, you know we just talked about change a minute ago. Change is a very difficult thing. I’m dealing with it constantly in my life. We’re all dealing with it. People don’t want to change and time goes on. But they needed Thad Jones and he

provided a boost for the band. They didn’t want to play his music, they claimed that Basie never liked his music anyway, that’s the reason he left, and he did leave because he wrote “Backbone,” and “Big Dipper” for them and it didn’t go over well. And he left and started his own band, which is fine. They said Basie didn’t like him because his stuff was getting too modern, that he shouldn’t be here now. The reality was people needed to have a name in front of the band. He made us rehearse. That band didn’t like to…
I like your impressions of him conducting. He had a certain, I mean, nobody conducted like him.
